summary: Describes a URN namespace created by Network Solutions for naming people and organizations, called the Personal Internet Name. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This describes a special kind of permanent name that a company made up for people and organizations.

questions: what is a personal internet name
subtitle: A persistent name for people and organizations that survives email and domain changes.

tldr.problem: People and organizations change email addresses, domain names, and even surnames, making it hard for online services to maintain long-term relationships and identify individuals uniquely across decades.
tldr.mechanism: Network Solutions created the PIN (Personal Internet Name) URN namespace, a flat space of unique persistent identifiers assigned by their registration system. Each person or organization gets one identifier that never changes.
tldr.outcome: Applications can reference people and organizations with a stable identifier similar to how domain names are used, but PIN URNs are resolved only by Network Solutions.

today: RFC 3043 is Informational. The PIN namespace was Network Solutions' proprietary effort, and the widespread adoption of RDF, FOAF, and social media profiles reduced the demand for such identifier systems.

sections.title: The Problem of Persistent Identity
sections.content:
Network Solutions' directory applications needed a way to uniquely identify people and organizations that would persist over decades. Email addresses, domain names, surnames, and even the DNS itself could disappear or change, but relationships and records needed to remain linkable to the right person or company.

A URN namespace (Uniform Resource Name) is a structured identifier system designed for exactly this: a standardized format for persistent, unique names that can be resolved in an open, non-proprietary way.
sections.plainLanguage: Businesses need a way to remember who you are for a very long time, even if you change your email or move.

sections.title: PIN URN Structure and Assignment
sections.content:
The PIN namespace is a flat, opaque space of alphanumeric identifiers with no knowable structure outside Network Solutions' internal systems. Network Solutions assigns identifiers from a numbering system that iterates from the last assigned number to guarantee uniqueness. Each identifier binds permanently to a person or organization, regardless of personal name changes, corporate restructuring, death, or dissolution.

Example PIN URNs: URN:pin:bs4321234, URN:pin:324kj5hkj45, URN:pin:mm2136.
sections.plainLanguage: Each person or organization gets a unique number. That number is yours forever, no matter what else changes.

sections.title: Resolution and Use
sections.content:
PIN URNs are case-insensitive and are resolved through URN resolvers run by Network Solutions. Resolving a PIN URN returns only information from an electronic proxy representing the person or organization, not the actual person. Other applications can adopt and reference PIN URNs in their own systems just as they adopt domain names from Network Solutions' database for use outside Network Solutions' applications.

Like ISBNs (maintained by specific entities but used widely), PIN URNs are intended for broad adoption wherever a well-maintained identifier for a person or organization is needed.
sections.plainLanguage: You can use someone's PIN number in your own program to link to information about them, just like how websites use domain names.
